Course Creation & Certification Requirements 2026-27

PowerSchool Professional Learning  ·  Office of Educator Development

Educator Certification Naming Conventions

Courses submitted for Educator Certification credit must follow ALSDE’s standard naming and description conventions so they can be reviewed and approved efficiently.

Title Format
LEA_Provider_Title of Professional Development
Examples of Titles
  • Baldwin County _ Learning Jumpstart _ Text-Dependent Writing Objectives
  • ALSDE _ ARI _ Dyslexia Awareness
  • Blount County _ Blount County Literacy Coach _ Science of Reading Foundations
  • Marion County _ Marion County CTE _ AI for Educators
  • Lee County _ Auburn University _ MTH 3311 Mathematics for Educators
Good LEA Examples
  • Montgomery County, Opelika City, Mobile County
Examples of What Not to Use
  • Montgomery Public Schools, Montgomery County Schools, MPS
Reminder: the LEA must still have the official transcript on file. A 3-semester-hour course is equivalent to 45 professional learning hours.
Course Description Format
Content Area: Description

The description should include the Subject Area Credit Type in bold at the beginning.

Example — English LA and Social Studies
  • This professional learning session is designed for high school educators to strengthen literacy while deepening content-area instruction. Participants will explore evidence-based instructional strategies that enhance reading comprehension, text analysis, historical thinking, source evaluation, and disciplinary writing. The session will focus on using literary and informational texts, primary and secondary sources, and inquiry-based learning to develop students’ critical thinking, argumentation, and evidence-based communication skills. Emphasis will also be placed on aligning instruction with Alabama English Language Arts and Social Studies standards to improve student achievement across both content areas.
Example — Educator Ethics
  • This course provides an in-depth study of ethical leadership and professional responsibility in education. Topics include the educator code of ethics, professional boundaries, student privacy and confidentiality, ethical use of technology and artificial intelligence, conflict of interest, mandatory reporting requirements, and equitable decision-making. Through case studies and reflective practice, participants develop the knowledge and skills necessary to navigate ethical dilemmas, maintain public trust, and support a positive school culture in accordance with state and professional standards.

Part 1 — Creating the Course

Part 1

Build the Course and Align to Standards

  1. 1Click the Professional Learning menu, then click the Build button on the left side of the screen.
  2. 2On the Build Courses and Sections screen, click the blue Build Course/Section button.
  3. 3Select Course Type (Instructor Led Course, Self Paced Course, or PLC) and click Continue.
  1. 4Give the course a Course Title (following the naming convention above) and choose the Office from the drop list — offices are listed alphabetically if you have access to more than one. Click Create.
  1. 5Enter a Course Description (following the description format above), including the Subject Area Credit Type in bold at the start.
  1. 6Choose the desired Credit Type and enter the number of units. Select the Credit Type carefully to match the subject-area content of the training being provided.
  2. 7Choose the Delivery Time Frame, Method of Delivery, and indicate whether the training is data informed/data driven and research based.
  3. 8If you are an Office Administrator in the Office where the course is being created, you can bypass approval via the Bypass Course Approval drop box (choose “Yes”). Otherwise, the course routes to a Final Approver.
  1. 9Choose ALSDE Default Survey for the Course Survey.
  2. 10Use the File Attachment feature to attach any desired documents to the course.
  3. 11Click the blue Next button in the bottom-right corner.
  4. 12Rubrics — Manage Course Alignment: Align the training to the Alabama Standards for Professional Learning (2024) / Alabama Core Teaching Standards. Ethics training must be aligned to the Alabama Educator Code of Ethics.
    • Select the standard set from the drop list and click Go.
    • Check the box for each Standard/Indicator to align, then click Align to Elements.
    • Selected Standards/Indicators display on the main screen — click Next.
  1. 13Choose the appropriate Course Tags (Subjects/Grade Levels) — optional — and click Next.
  2. 14Visibility: use Manage Location to control who can find and register for the course. Statewide courses display AL; school- or district-level courses default to that school/district.
  3. 15Click Add Section to begin creating sections for the course.
  1. 16Section Creation — Section Details:
    • Enter a Section Name and click Add Section. Notes (including hyperlinks) can be added in the Notes box.
    • Contact Person — the person responsible for the training; include their email.
    • Presenter — the person conducting the training.
    • Delivery Format — choose from the drop list.
    • Instructors — add via the Add Instructors button; instructors manage the section roster, print sign-in sheets, mark attendance, and award credit. Consider adding yourself for easier access to rosters later.
    • Location Settings — a location is required; indicate if the section is online.
    • Registration Settings — maximum participants; End of Registration Date (defaults to the Start Date if left blank); Release to Catalog date/time.
    • Waitlist Settings — optionally enable a waitlist and set a maximum size.
  1. 17Section Creation — Class Times:
    • Under the Class Time tab, confirm the toggle for “Populate start and end date based on class times” is in the green (on) position.
    • Click Add Class Times to add the start date and time. For multi-day trainings, click Add Class Time again for each additional day.
  2. 18With Section Details and Class Times complete, click Submit Course and Section.
If you were able to bypass approval, the course becomes available for registration on the date/time indicated. If not, a Final Approver in that Office must approve the course and section(s).

Part 2 — Approving Courses

Part 2

Review and Approve Submitted Courses

  1. 1Under the Professional Learning menu, click Approvals → My Pending Approvals to see courses and sections awaiting approval (also visible on the Dashboard). Click a title to open it.
  2. 2On the Course or Section Details screen, review all details, then click Review Comments in the upper-right corner.
  3. 3In the Tier 1 Approval window, select Approved and click Submit. If revisions are needed, select Needs Revision, enter an explanation, and click Submit — the original creator is emailed and can revise/resubmit under Build.

If you have questions or suggestions about this process, please contact us at pladmin@alsde.edu.
